source.title: Source spreadsheet
source.cell: Iron CEA, TA cost per person!B36

rows.explainer: We see increases in IQ after supplementation for less than 1 year. It could be that there's a linear effect (e.g. one year of supplementation raises IQ by 5 points, 2 years raises IQ by 10 points). That's extremely implausible though. More likely, going from low haemoglobin levels to normal haemoglobin levels leads to an IQ increase of a couple points. I would guess that those cognitive benefits remain as long as someone is non-anemic and mostly disappear if haemoglobin levels return to the initial low levels. More details here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/15ifHdYl-mI6ZF_SgksADD3myusxya3ZBYrPHLKt9_ao/edit?usp=sharing
